_comment_last_release_sha: The v0.9.0 release commit. Nothing before it is scanned for conventional
commits, which stops a Release-As footer being honoured a second time.
e1ac251 carries 'Release-As: 0.8.0' and that footer is permanent in the
history, so release-please proposed 0.8.0 again after 0.9.0 had shipped:
a pull request whose own compare link read v0.9.0...v0.8.0 and which
would have downgraded the manifest if anybody had merged it.
Move this to each new release commit only if the same thing recurs.
This read 88cacf6ae4ff21c30dd7bbfc61ba9c8b96c65b8f for five releases and
no such commit exists: the GitHub API answers 422 for it, and so does
`git cat-file`. Only the short prefix was right. A sha that matches no
commit never stops the scan, so the bound did nothing and 0.8.0 was
proposed four more times, in #24, #26, #29 and #32. The real v0.9.0
release commit is below; check a replacement with `git cat-file -e`
